newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's net int'l reserves rise to $9.310 billion.
newsitem.headline: Peru's net int'l reserves rise to $9.310 billion.

text.p: Peru's Central Reserve Bank said Friday its net international reserves rose $138 million to $9.310 billion by April 9 from $9.173 billion at the end of March.
The bank did not specify in its weekly report on which date the latest reserve figure was taken.
It said the reason for the rise was a $137 million increase in bank deposits.
Peru's foreign reserves have grown by $770 million so far this year.
The central bank also said its foreign exchange position, or total liquidity minus short and long-term debt obligations, was $1.714 billion by April 9, down $10 million from the end of March.
Peru's reserves ended 1996 at $8.540 billion. The government estimates the country's international reserves will rise above $10 billion by mid-1998.
